newsitem.title: INDIA: India planning body proposes 7 pct annual growth.
newsitem.headline: India planning body proposes 7 pct annual growth.

text.p: India's Planning Commission said on Thursday Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's cabinet had accepted its proposal for a 7 percent annual growth rate for the country's 9th five-year plan starting on April 1, 1997.

"India will aim for an average growth rate of 7 percent in the 9th five-year plan," a commission statement said. The plan has to be endorsed by the National Development Council, which includes all the states' chief ministers, to become effective.
The NDC will meet on January 16.
Economic growth was targeted at 5.9 percent in the previous five year plan covering 1992/97.
The Planning Commission has also set a 9.3 percent annual growth target for industrial growth for the next five years.
It set the target for annual export growth at 14.5 percent for the 1997-2002 period, compared with 11.4 percent in the previous five-year plan.
Annual import growth was targeted at 15.3 percent, compared with 13.6 percent in previous plan.
